STEP 1 - Vessel type: square flat plate. It has a raised rim band and a flat centre with no deep inner wall, and the food sits on the surface.

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type cue: square plates are typically 20-30 cm. This one looks medium-sized, around 22-24 cm.
b) Reference cue: the strawberries are about 3-4 cm across. The plate spans roughly 6-7 strawberry widths across its top edge, which gives about 21-26 cm. The broccoli floret (about 4 cm) at the top-left is about 1 floret-width from the rim to the wrapped stem, consistent with the same range.
Reconciled width: about 23 cm, so area = 23² = 529 cm².

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Broccoli: a cluster of about 3 florets covering roughly 8% of the plate area. Footprint = 0.08 × 529 ≈ 42 cm². Thickness ≈ 2.5 cm (a floret pile, one to two florets high, averaged). Volume ≈ 42 × 2.5 × 0.5 (mound factor) ≈ 53 ml. Density 0.6 g/ml (chopped vegetable) gives ≈ 32 g.
- Strawberries: about 7 slices (halves/quarters) covering roughly 12% of the plate area. Footprint = 0.12 × 529 ≈ 63 cm². Thickness ≈ 1.5 cm (sliced berries, partly stacked). Volume ≈ 63 × 1.5 × 0.6 ≈ 57 ml. Density 0.6 g/ml gives ≈ 34 g. Adding the hidden pieces underneath the stacked slices, round to ≈ 45 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: no base layer is visible. The plate centre is empty, so no hidden food is added.

STEP 5 - Energy:
- Broccoli, raw/steamed: about 34 kcal per 100 g.
- Strawberries, raw: about 32 kcal per 100 g.

Totals: broccoli ≈ 32 g → ≈ 11 kcal; strawberries ≈ 45 g → ≈ 14 kcal. Total food ≈ 77 g, ≈ 25 kcal.
